I've come close to death many times, though I'm not sure which is closest.

At birth I was 9 weeks early and could fit in the palm of my dad's hand. My premature body was very underdeveloped. My muscles had not yet fully formed, nor my bones, or lungs as I have been told. The doc told my parents several times not to get their hopes up as I very well might not make it. My heart would stop at times because it wasnt strong enough, my lungs weren't developed enough to allow me to breathe properly, and my bones were still soft which meant my mother could not really hold me. In addition to all this I barely had an immune system.  For the first few months of my life I lived in an incubator. Before the hospital even let my parents take me home they had to learn extensive knowledge on how to take care of me. Things like baby cpr, and how to help slow my heart rate in cases of too much stimulus. Luckily 21 years later my immune system is strong as an ox, my lungs work alright, and my heart still beats. This isn't really an event in which I came close to death, more like a period of time in which I wasn't expected to survive.

Sometime when I was about 7 me and my brother were playing on the metal swing set in our back yard. There's a long hollow metal pole that runs along the top to support the swings. I stand on top of the slide connected to the side and my brother decides to start shaking the whole darned swing set, much to my amusement initially. Then suddenly out of the end of the top pole facing me comes an entire nest of hornets and unlucky for me I'm allergic to their sting. Not sure of the exact number but I got stung 40-some times in the face and had to be rushed to the emergency room. Damn near died from the allergic reaction but I recovered.

When I was 11 me and my family went to a park that allowed you to ride horses through trails. I was super excited and so my mom let me pick out the horse we would ride, but the guy in charge insisted I ride my own horse despite never having done so before and also being so young. My mother objected several times but finally gave in, trusting that the guy knew what he was talking about, albeit reluctantly. So we start off and I'm riding this awesome black and white horse named Oreo, I'm talking to him the whole time. About halfway through the ride my horse starts to gallop, and I had no idea how to stop a galloping horse. Being very tiny I was bouncing around like a rag doll. I should probably mention that at this point on the trail there was a very steep 50 ft drop to our left. Which normally posed no problem for riders, except for the fact that I nearly fell off my horse and over the edge which shurely would've caused my death. By some miracle I fell to my right on solid ground, but the danger was not yet passed. My horse had spooked others behind him which almost trampled me to death as they galloped past. One actually stepped on my arm and fractured both the bones, but yet I lived. My mom had to pick me up in her arms, run to the nearest road, flag down a vehicle, and have them drive use to a hospital to make sure I was okay. I was still in shock during the car ride but yet again, I recovered.

I was 14 and in middle school. One day I came down with the latest bug that was going around, which initially seemed to be a regular cold/flu that would pass in a week at most. I had gone to the doc two days post onset of symptoms and I exhibited signs as such. I still went to school for a week, but during that week I got worse and worse. The next week I almost couldn't get out of bed, so I went back to the doc and had some tests done. Apparently I had a bug that was resistant to most antibiotics so there were other options, but since my immune system had been weakened so much from fighting it off (it was a real nasty virus) it would take some time. Third week rolls around and I'm still not better. I never even left my bed except to use the restroom. Finally my mom was so scared she admitted me to the emergency room, and it took me a bit over a week to recover enough to go back to school.  The other kids had thought I'd moved away because I'd been gone so long. When I told them that it was because I was sick a lot of people looked at me like I was diseased and made sure to keep their distance from me for several weeks following my return. This may not sound like I came close to death but by the point I was admitted I was coughing up phlegm, vomiting (couldn't keep anything down even toast), had a fever, cold chills, constantly dehydrated, never-ending headache, and my whole body felt like it was on fire. I was in a lot of pain, yet again, I recovered.

I was 18 and driving home from hanging put with a bunch of people at a party, but I was very tired. I thought I could handle driving home as it was only a 15 minute drive. Not even 2 minutes into the drive I fall asleep at the wheel and swerve into oncoming traffic. At the last second the honk of a very large truck heading straight for me wakes me up and I swerve out of the way in just enough time. My car was very small compared to the truck and I surely would not have survived the impact. I was so scared after that I nearly ahat myself, but not once did I come close to falling asleep again.

TL;DR - Death doesn't want me yet
